haiku-low.q1: Login uses the linked sub and calls start_session for that user, even though the Google email changed. No email match is needed.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter that account's password on the confirm-password page. Only then is the identity inserted and start_session called.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password counts as a failed login. The 5th locks the account, deletes the pending link and shows 'Account temporarily locked'. Earlier failures show the page again.
haiku-low.q4: No matching user: create a user with no password and verified email, insert identity, start session. Email not verified: refuse, point to email and password, create nothing.
haiku-low.q5: Both fail with no change. At 12 minutes the state has expired (10-minute lifetime). A second load finds nothing because the attempt is deleted on first use. Error page shown.
haiku-low.q6: It calls start_session, creating a sessions row and setting the sid cookie, the same as password login. What happens to an existing sid cookie: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required. If the sub is linked to anyone, or the user already has a Google account, settings refuses with a message and nothing changes.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis, in an attempt holding state, nonce, PKCE verifier and start point, for 10 minutes. The callback deletes it when used, or it expires.
haiku-low.q9: In a Redis pending link naming the sub and user X. How the browser refers to it: NOT STATED. Deleted when the user confirms, the account locks, or after 10 minutes.
haiku-low.q10: In the user_identities table (user_id, sub). Unique constraints on sub and user_id enforce one Google account per user and one user per Google account.
haiku-low.q11: The user returns to the starting point with 'Google sign-in failed, try again'. Nothing is created and the user can retry. Automatic retry of the exchange: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q12: The attempt stores whether it started at login or settings, and the callback follows that path. How the callback confirms the same signed-in user: NOT STATED.

sonnet.q1: They are signed in as the linked user via start_session, because the identity is matched by sub and the changed Google email does not matter.
sonnet.q2: The user must confirm the existing account's password on the confirm-password page (a pending link is saved in Redis first). Only after a correct password does the identity get inserted and start_session is called.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password counts as a failed login. The fifth failure locks the account (15 minutes), deletes the pending link, and shows 'Account temporarily locked'. No identity is inserted.
sonnet.q4: If the email matches no user, a user is created with no password and a verified email, an identity is inserted, and start_session is called. If email_verified is false, sign-in is refused, the user is pointed to email and password, and nothing is created.
sonnet.q5: The state is unknown, expired or used, so an error page is shown and nothing changes. The attempt lives 10 minutes and is deleted on first use, so a second load of the callback finds nothing.
sonnet.q6: It is the same kind of session as a password login: start_session creates a sessions row and sets the sid cookie. NOT STATED for what happens to a sid cookie the browser already had.
sonnet.q7: No password is asked and the emails need not match. If the sub is already linked to anyone (or the user already has a Google account), the link is refused with a message on the settings page and nothing changes.
sonnet.q8: They are kept in a Redis attempt, together with the starting point, for 10 minutes. The callback looks it up by state and deletes it in the same operation, or it expires after 10 minutes.
sonnet.q9: It is held in a Redis pending link entry (this sub is waiting for the password of user X). It lives 10 minutes. It is deleted when the user confirms, when the account locks, or when it expires. NOT STATED for how the browser refers to it.
sonnet.q10: It is stored in the user_identities table (user_id, sub). Unique constraints on both sub and user_id enforce one Google account per user and one user per Google account.
sonnet.q11: The user is returned to the starting point with 'Google sign-in failed, try again'. Nothing is created, and the user can retry manually. The document does not mention any automatic retry of the exchange.
sonnet.q12: The attempt stored in Redis records where it started (login or settings), and the callback reads that. For settings links, the identity is inserted for the signed-in user. NOT STATED for how the callback verifies that the signed-in user is the one who started the attempt.
